div.l: Whiche þat hath þᵉ shorteste shal by gynne
¶ Sir knyght qduod he my maist̉er and my lord
Now draweth cut for þat is myn acord
Comethe nere qduod he my lady prioresse
And ȝe Sir Clerk lat be ȝoure Shamfastnes
Ne studieth nought lay hond to eủery man
A · noon to draw eủery wight by gane
And Shortli for to tellen as it was
Were it by auenture or Sort or cas
Þᵉ Sothe is þis þᵉ Cut fel to the knyght
Of whiche ful blith ⁊and glad was eủery wight
And tellen he moste his tale as it was reson
By forward and by composicion
As ȝe haue herd what nedith wordes moo
And whan þis godman Saugh þat is was so
As he þat wys was and obedient
To kepen his forward bi his fre assent
He seide sithen · I shal by gynne þe game
What welcome be the Cut a goddes name
Now let vs Ride and herketh what I seie
And with þat word we riden forth oure weie
And he by gan wᵗith riȝt a merie chere
His tale a noon and seide as ȝe maye here

Iamqꝫue domos patⁱrias scithice post asꝑpera gentis
prelia laurig̉ero ⁊et c̉etera
Here endith þe prologꝰue This line and the next are written less formally than the rest of the page and may have been added later.
Here bygynnyth þᵉ ꝓprologꝰue of of þᵉ knyȝtes tale This line and the previous one are written less formally than the rest of the page and may have been added later.
Whilom was as old stories tellen vs
Ther was a · duk þat hight theseus
Of Athenes he was lord and goủernour
And in his tyme swiche a Conquerour
Þat gretter was noon vnder the sonne
Ful monye a riche contre hade he wone
What with his wisdom and his Chiualrye
He conquered al the regne of femynye
And whilom was I clepid scithia
And weddet þe quene ypolita
And brought hir home wᵗith hym in his contre
Wᵗith moche glorie and grete solempnite
